How i would expect the json file to look like for sdo batch layer 

streams.json

sdo{
    "partition_granularity": "year",
    "anchor": "end",
    "available methods": ["sdo_access", "sdo_campania_xml"] << this link works in my brain but maybe is probably better implemented in methods so methods can know what kind of datastream they are linked to
}


{
  "sdo_access": {
    "stream": "sdo", << this is the link
    "type": "access_db", << descriptive i suppose
    "input_type": "file", 
    "table": "EXPORT_TABLE", <<not sure what this is for and why all caps
    "components":[
    "TblScheda", "TblSchedaDiagnosi", "TblSchedaProcedure", "TblSchedaTrasferimenti"
] <<< these are the tables we need to import from the access object. i think its better to state them here
    "mapping": {
      "c_NumeroScheda": "c_NumeroScheda" <<< not sure what this is for
    }
    "primary_table": "TblScheda", << this may or may not be important, dont understandits implications
    "identity_keys": ["c_NumeroScheda", "c_CodPresidio", "c_AzUSSL"], << maybe this is related to primary_table? 
    "partition_column": "d_DataDimissione",
    "pseudonymize": ["c_CodicePaziente", "c_CodiceMadre"],
    "skip": ["v_Nome", "v_Cognome"]
  },
  "sdo_campania_xml": { << while this example is almost empty for this method this should be similar to access. the difference is that targeted columns for identity keys and pseudonymization would be different 
    "stream": "sdo",
    "type": "xml",
    "input_type": "directory",
    "components": {
      "TblAnagrafica": "*_A.xml",
      "TblRicoveroICD9": "*_B.xml",
      "TblRicoveroICD10": "*_D.xml",
      "TblProcedures": "*_C.xml"
    }
  }
}
